test_name: STDB reducer string args sent as null - 5c9a0a6c-7f02-49f4-883f-59111ba6e22f
summary: The audit found three places that could send null text to the multiplayer database (STDB), which crashes the request. All three are fixed. (1) An expired Unity login session used to send four nulls to the Login reducer. It now fails the join with a clear 'Player session has expired' error. (2) Before redeeming, a store purchase missing its SKU, order id or receipt (possible with Meta's raw purchase data) is now logged and left unconsumed instead of being sent. (3) A Steam store user without an id is now logged and skipped instead of being bound with null. The project compiles clean, and an editor test confirmed the redeem guard rejects null Meta purchases without calling the server. The expired-login and Steam paths could not be reproduced in the editor, so they were checked in code only.
instructions:
TASK: STDB String nullability audit

DESCRIPTION:
See claude conversation "STDB String nullability audit"

\
Context for Junior dev:\
\
I'll start with the project's mandatory orientation step, then sweep the Rust reducers for non-nullable `String` params.

Now let me verify the mechanism client-side and find the C# call sites.

Now let me read each client-path call site with its guards.

Now tracing upstream callers for the highest-risk args (platform-sourced and optional-by-design values).

Found the first real one. Let me check the remaining client paths.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`\
The audit surface is defined by three layers, and only the middle one is greppable: Rust reducer/procedure signatures (`String` vs `Option<String>`), the C# choke point (`SpacetimeDBConnector` + `AsyncReducers.g.cs` — a pure pass-through, no coalescing of its own), and the actual value origin. Only the third layer decides whether a bug exists, so every `String` param has to be traced to where the value is *born*. Note that `#[spacetimedb::procedure]` args have the identical hazard — the IAP path is procedures, not reducers, so a reducer-only sweep would have missed them entirely.\
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## \[SUMMARY\]

Swept all 166 reducers + 4 procedures → 60 have `String`/`Vec<String>` params → traced every non-generated C# call site to its value origin.

**3 findings. 1 confirmed crash, 2 unguarded external boundaries.** Everything else is genuinely guarded.

---

## 🔴 #1 — `Login` sends 4 nulls when the Unity auth session is expired

[UnityMultiplayerLogin.cs:137](https://claude.ai/epitaxy/Assets/__Multiplayer/_Tech/Scripts/Login/Unity/UnityMultiplayerLogin.cs:137)

```
if (AuthenticationService.Instance.IsExpired) {
    logger.ZLogError("Player session has expired");
    return (null, null, null, null);      // ← all four
}
```

[MultiplayerDB.cs:37](https://claude.ai/epitaxy/Assets/__Multiplayer/_Tech/Scripts/Database/MultiplayerDB.cs:37) destructures and forwards them unchecked → `LoginAsync` → `Reducers.Login(bundleCode, null, null, null, null)`. Rust side ([connection.rs:99](https://claude.ai/epitaxy/Cloud%20Code%20Projects/SpacetimeDB-Server-Rust/src/reducers/connection.rs:99)): `unityPlayerId: String, name: String, platformUsername: String, normalConnectionData: String` — four non-nullable params, 4/4 null.

`ZLogError` then returning a poison tuple reads as handled, but nothing downstream checks it. This is the exact shape of the original bug, on the single most-travelled reducer in the game.

**Adjacent, same root cause, different failure mode:** two lines below, `GetSanitizedPlayerName(PlayerPrefs.GetString("MPName", AuthenticationService.Instance.PlayerName))` — [IUdStoreManager.cs:51](https://claude.ai/epitaxy/Assets/Scripts/StoreManagers/Shared/IUdStoreManager.cs:51) does `playerName.IndexOf('#')` with no null check, so a null `PlayerName` + unset pref NREs there instead of at the wire.

## 🟠 #2 — Meta IAP passes SDK-supplied strings raw into 4 procedure params

[MetaIAPService.cs:165-170](https://claude.ai/epitaxy/Assets/Scripts/StoreManagers/Oculus/MetaIAPService.cs:165) → `PlatformOrderId = p.ID`, `ReceiptBlob = p.ID`, `Sku = p.Sku` straight off the Oculus purchase object. [UdStoreManager_Impl.cs:768](https://claude.ai/epitaxy/Assets/Scripts/StoreManagers/UdStoreManager/UdStoreManager_Impl.cs:768) forwards all of them to `RedeemPurchase(handle, platform, sku, platformOrderId, receiptBlob)` — 4 non-nullable `String` procedure params, zero coalescing in between.

What makes this stand out: **every other branch coalesces explicitly.** Steam writes `ReceiptBlob = ""` ([SteamIAPService.cs:167](https://claude.ai/epitaxy/Assets/Scripts/StoreManagers/Steam/SteamIAPService.cs:167)), MicroTxn passes `receiptBlob: ""` with a comment naming this exact hazard ([UdStoreManager_Impl.cs:723](https://claude.ai/epitaxy/Assets/Scripts/StoreManagers/UdStoreManager/UdStoreManager_Impl.cs:723)), Mock writes a literal. Meta is the one path handing platform strings through untouched. I can't prove Meta's SDK returns null `ID`/`Sku` from here — but it's an unguarded external boundary, and it fails inside the redeem-retry loop.

## 🟠 #3 — `SetPlatformIdentity` Steam branch: `storeUser.Value.id` unchecked

[UdStoreManager_Impl.cs:840](https://claude.ai/epitaxy/Assets/Scripts/StoreManagers/UdStoreManager/UdStoreManager_Impl.cs:840) → `platformUserId = storeUser.Value.id;` → :848 `SetPlatformIdentity(purchase.Platform, platformUserId)`, both non-nullable.

The `Oculus` case above it reads the *same field* but runs it through `ulong.TryParse` and bails on failure — which makes it null-safe by accident, not by intent. The `Steam`/`SteamInventory` case passes it through. Reachable if `CachedUserInfo` is ever populated with a name but no id. Worth a look given your working tree is mid-change on `IStoreAvatarFetcher` / `StoreAvatars` / both store managers.

---

## \[CLEAN\] verified guarded, not assumed

Path Guard `SetActiveLoadoutPaintUrls`, `SetActiveLoadoutDesignBundleUrl` `?? ""` in connector `ReportPlayer` reason/code `?? ""` + `code = ""` `FindRoom` groupToken/levelGroup/privateKey all 3 resolvers coalesce — **load-bearing**, see below `excludedRoomId`, `JoinSpecificRoom`, `ReportRoomState` `""` default; else STDB row strings `cageId`, `elevatorId` `[SerializeField] string` — Unity never deserializes null `UpdateProfile` `IsNullOrWhiteSpace` guard; TMP `.text` `ClaimBadge`, `ClaimBlingDecals` literals + config; explicit `m.badgeId != null`; list null/empty guard `ReportStat`/`ReportStatReset`/`ActivateBetStat` STDB row strings `NotifyRegion` `?? ""` at [MultiplayerScene.cs:265](https://claude.ai/epitaxy/Assets/__Multiplayer/_Tech/Scripts/Core/MultiplayerScene.cs:265) Editor tools (PlayerDevTab, StockCuration, Globals, AdminGate) `IsNullOrEmpty` preconditions or TextField `""`

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`\
`FindRoom` deserves calling out as a near-miss that holds. `MultiplayerSpawnElevator` exposes `GroupToken`/`LevelGroup`/`PrivateKey` as `_row?.X` ([MultiplayerSpawnElevator.cs:92-94](https://claude.ai/epitaxy/Assets/__Multiplayer/_Tech/Scripts/LevelLogic/Elevator/MultiplayerSpawnElevator.cs:92)) — genuinely null before the elevator row syncs — and `MultiplayerElevatorTeleportDetector` feeds all three straight into `FindMatchAsync`. What saves it is that `ResolveLevelGroup`/`ResolvePrivateKey`/`GenerateNewGroupToken` each test `IsNullOrEmpty` and substitute. Those resolvers exist for override precedence, so their null protection is incidental: anyone "simplifying" them into plain `??` defaults or bypassing them reopens a crash three files away. Worth a comment if you touch that code.\
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

## \[NOTE\]

`SpacetimeDB.BSATN.String` ships as a compiled DLL ([spacetimedb.bsatn.runtime/2.2.0](https://claude.ai/epitaxy/CustomPackages/STDB/packages/spacetimedb.bsatn.runtime)), so I did not independently re-verify the null-throws claim — I took it as given. It's corroborated in-tree by the two comments at the already-fixed sites ("the reducer's reason is a non-nullable string", "The procedure arg is a non-nullable BSATN string, so null would throw").

## \[NEXT\]

Nothing changed — this was a check. Two options if you want #1 closed:

1. **Point fix** — coalesce at [MultiplayerDB.cs:37](https://claude.ai/epitaxy/Assets/__Multiplayer/_Tech/Scripts/Database/MultiplayerDB.cs:37), or better, make the `IsExpired` branch throw instead of returning a poison tuple.
2. **Structural** — the connector coalesces in 3 of \~25 string-passing wrappers, i.e. per-author discipline. Coalescing inside the `AsyncReducersManualGenerator~` codegen would cover every reducer path at once, though not `conn.Procedures.*` (the IAP calls bypass it).

Say which and I'll do it.
